data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only when the test would fail without the subject's independent contribution; in the shown-to-fail-first installation, the test fails before the mutation is even applied, so the test cannot constrain the mutation\u2014it can only describe the installation ritual's failure mode.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the test were run without the shown-to-fail-first ritual and still passed, the constraint hypothesis would be supported.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3 survivors were tested under a different installation order and still survived, the ritual hypothesis would be weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutation were applied after the test passed, the test would constrain the mutation directly.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The shown-to-fail-first ritual pre-commits the test to a failure state, so any later passage is a property of the ritual's completion, not of the mutation. The 3-of-26 result is the number of mutations that survived the ritual's completion, not the number that survived the test.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
